rationale: Neither candidate design can be chosen honestly yet. A comparison of existing records depends on INR data whose completeness is unknown and is confounded by site; a randomised comparison of new referrals avoids confounding but needs about 17 months of referrals and training of main-site pharmacists on the software. The recorded search returned nothing to guide the choice. The simplest honest step is a four-week profile of the records, already approved, after which the design is revisited with a fixed rule.
alternatives: Records comparison of time in range adjusted for case mix (only if the profile shows calculable time in range for most patients at every clinic)
Randomised comparison of new referrals between the two approaches (if the records are unfit or confounding cannot be handled)
Standardise on the software now without a local comparison (refused: no retrieved evidence and no local data)
guidelines: RECORD, if the records comparison is chosen
CONSORT, if the randomised comparison is chosen
whyNotMoreComplex: Designing both comparisons in full now would spend pharmacist time on a plan the data may not support; the profile is small, approved and decisive.

decision.statement: Defer the choice between a records comparison and a randomised comparison until a four-week profile of INR and dose records shows whether time in range can be calculated at all three clinics.
decision.question: Which design, if any, should compare the paper nomogram with the computer-assisted dosing tool?

criteria.text: The profile shows time in range calculable for most patients at every clinic, with completeness similar across sites.
The anticoagulation committee standardises on one approach before the profile is complete.

gates.requirement: Clinic manager approval to profile INR and dose records for completeness
gates.evidence: Approval ACM-2026-14 dated 2026-09-08, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Standardise on the software now without a local comparison
Start the records comparison immediately and accept the risk of incomplete data
decision.note: No ledger claim exists because the recorded search returned no records and the investigator confirmed it empty; the decision rests on the investigator's local facts. The recommendation is null on purpose: the family stays unresolved until the profile is done.

summary: No design recommended yet; the decision defers the choice to a four-week records profile with an approval already in place.
